effort: Express leg force rapidly against manageable external resistance while keeping the foot and pelvis organized.
brief: The limiting demand is maintaining fast force expression when an implement adds resistance. E1 gives a very small externally loaded takeoff exposure; landmine squat and split-hinge drives offer guided planted-foot force, supported hip thrust addresses hip finish, seated thigh lift addresses leg recovery, and straight-knee heel rise addresses ankle force. The latter five have no flight. Light ankle and offset-trunk work precede familiar challenging strength.
marker: Across two sets of two jumps, record secure DB handling, a crisp takeoff and a controlled two-foot landing under the body. Choose the smallest useful load that does not visibly disrupt speed or position; no universal kilograms, velocity target or maximum-load test. If loaded execution is unsuitable, the unloaded route is the correct recorded result.
review: Class 8 prescribed 21 landings and seven primary rounds with a new step-up. No actual response is known. Class 9 reduces jump landings to four, replaces most impact with short resisted rapid-force tasks and retains seven primary rounds. External resistance is a conditional task constraint, not proof of strength gained over eight written classes.
sequence: Only E1 includes flight and it receives two tiny sets. Every subsequent row uses a light implement for fast concentric force with controlled return; stop well before fatigue reduces speed.

E.name: Loaded Squat Jump — light dumbbells
E.job: Main task: retain coordinated takeoff and receiving while a small external mass adds force demand.
E.cue: Very light DBs at sides, one shallow dip, modest vertical jump, land both feet under the hips and hold 2 s with arms quiet. Never throw or drop the DBs. Use unloaded jumps instead if grip, landing or speed is compromised.

E.name: Landmine Squat-to-Forefoot Drive — no flight
E.job: Express coordinated hip/knee/ankle extension against a guided forward-up load without another landing.
E.cue: Secure landmine and suitable light bar/load; both hands hold the end at chest. From a shallow squat drive tall onto forefeet in one continuous rise, keep forefeet grounded, then lower over 2 s. No overhead press or arm push; reduce load if the bar controls posture.

E.name: Split-Stance Landmine Hinge Drive
E.job: Direct fast hip-extension force through an asymmetric base while the guided implement limits unnecessary swing travel.
E.cue: Light landmine end held in both hands low in front, short split stance. Hinge with softly bent knees, drive hips tall quickly and return over 2 s. Both feet stay planted, no arm curl or pelvis twist; shorten hinge/rack distance for trunk loss.

E.name: Explosive Hip Thrust — light dumbbell, bench supported
E.job: Accelerate terminal hip extension through a supported range against a small external load.
E.cue: Upper back on a stable suitable bench, feet grounded, hands secure a light pelvic DB. Drive up quickly to ribs/pelvis alignment, lower over 2 s; do not launch the implement or arch the back. Use less load/range if speed or control fades.

E.name: Seated Dumbbell Hip Flexion — fast thigh lift
E.job: Accelerate the thigh against light resistance while the supported pelvis removes a balance limit.
E.cue: Sit tall with foot grounded, hands securing a light DB above the knee. Lift the thigh a small amount quickly, lower over 2 s without leaning back. No loose weight on a foot; reduce load/range for pelvic movement.

E.name: Standing Calf Raise — fast concentric, supported single leg
E.job: Express fast plantarflexion through the straight-knee stance configuration without leaving the floor.
E.cue: One light DB, stable hand support, near-straight soft knee. Rise quickly through the forefoot, return over 2 s; forefoot never leaves. Use bodyweight instead if external load changes speed or ankle alignment.

S.name: Seated Band Ankle Inversion
S.job: Light medial-ankle/foot control to preserve the arch platform under resisted leg drive.
S.cue: Seated, target heel grounded; loop a light band around forefoot and hold ends slightly to the outside of that foot. Turn forefoot gently inward against tension for 2 s and return 2 s without rotating the knee. Reduce tension for whole-leg movement; gentle hand resistance may replace the band at the same dose.

S.name: Split-Stance Suitcase Hold — light dumbbell
S.job: Light anti-side-bend trunk/pelvic strengthening for transferring force through an asymmetrically loaded stance.
S.cue: One light DB beside the body, opposite foot slightly forward; keep both feet grounded and ribs over pelvis. Hold tall without leaning or shrugging, breathe easily. Switch arm and lead foot for the other side; use less weight for sway.

P.name: Split Squat — two dumbbells at sides
P.cue: Floor split stance, front foot planted, pelvis square; lower 2 s and rise firmly for 1 s. Reduce load/range for collapse or balance loss. Use one DB with stable hand support instead of two unsupported DBs if needed; counts stay the same.
P.job: Retain the familiar main stance-force anchor while external-speed tasks change.

P.name: Romanian Deadlift — two dumbbells
P.cue: Soft knees, hips back, DBs close; lower 3 s and rise in 1 s. Stop the descent before back rounding; reduce load/range if the hinge becomes spinal movement.
P.job: Supply one challenging hip-hinge set after the limited fast hinge/thrust work.

P.name: Bent-Knee Soleus Raise — seated dumbbells
P.cue: Both legs together, knees near 90°, heels start on floor, hands secure DBs on lower thighs above knees. Rise 1 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s. Reduce load for bounce/lost heel height. If bench fit is unsuitable, use supported standing bent-knee calf raises instead, same reps/rest, and log changed knee angle.
P.job: Maintain controlled knee-flexed ankle force alongside the fast straight-knee drill.

P.name: Standing Dumbbell Calf Raise — supported single leg
P.cue: Work from floor, near-straight soft knee, one DB and stable hand support. Rise 1 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s. Reduce load or use bodyweight for lost range; use 1 × 8 bilateral instead of per-leg work if even unilateral bodyweight is too demanding, with 1 × 4 bilateral preparation.
P.job: Keep the established controlled straight-knee strength role; this is a separate slower, heavier performance from E6.

P.name: Glute Bridge Walkout
P.cue: Keep a floor bridge while four small alternating heel steps go out and four return; eight steps at about 1 s each = one full cycle. Choose reach so four cycles are challenging with 2–3 whole cycles available. Shorten reach for pelvic sag or cramping; do not add steps or cycles.
P.job: Retain knee-flexor strength through changing heel lever without another loaded standing hinge.

P.name: Supine Band-resisted Hip Flexion
P.cue: Secure loop band around both forefeet; nonworking leg straight with heel grounded. Flex working hip/knee toward thigh-vertical in 2 s, hold 1 s, return 2 s without arching or moving the anchor heel. Reduce tension/range for pelvic tilt. If a secure loop is unavailable, use seated DB hip flexion instead with hands securing the DB above the knee: same dose/rest, small controlled thigh lift; preparation unloaded.
P.job: Maintain supported challenging hip-flexor strength, distinct from E5's small fast light-load dose.

equipment: E1 requires secure light DB handling and prior current unloaded jump control; use unloaded countermovement jumps instead at the same 2 × 2/rest if needed. E2/E3 require a secured landmine with a manageable total bar/handle mass; availability does not prove a light enough setup. Use a light goblet squat-to-forefoot drive instead of E2, same 1 × 4/no flight, or a light two-hand DB split-stance hinge drive instead of E3, same 1 × 3 per lead side/no flight. E4 uses a light loaded floor bridge instead if bench fit fails, same 1 × 4/rest, changed range recorded. E5 can be unloaded instead if no safe small DB fits; it remains a rapid thigh-lift task. If even unloaded controlled flight or implement handling is unsuitable, record modified/incomplete work rather than adding contacts.
count_note: Only E1 has flight: four two-foot landings, eight individual foot contacts. Other rapid work totals four landmine squat drives, six split-hinge drives, four supported hip drives, eight thigh lifts and eight heel rises; these are 30 nonflight force efforts, not 30 jump contacts. Speed-task loads differ from primary-strength loads, and no rep is counted in both blocks. All stated replacements preserve the default landing count but change resistance/support.
novelty: The new default task constraints are a small held jump load, guided triple extension, guided split-hinge force, bench-supported rapid hip finish, a secured seated thigh load and fast straight-knee force without impact. These are openly related resisted/support variants, not six unrelated families. The fast heel-rise action was already a Class 2 contingency, so it is not new for an athlete who actually used that route; that usage is unknown. Simpler substitutes can recur deliberately.
audit: Rejected Olympic-lift catches, heavy loaded jumps and loose DB-on-foot drills. Restricted loaded flight to four events and defined secure holds/grounded feet for all other tasks. Kept each overlapping fast hip/ankle task to a few light reps and main strength to seven rounds; slowed challenging sets are separate performances. Landmine mass and bench fit remain delivery checks with practical substitutes.
progression: A heavier implement is not the goal. Select load for fast controlled execution today, and hold it until actual speed/control and recovery are reported. Do not advance explosive and strength loads together automatically. Class 10 should consolidate repeatable low-cost force tasks, using familiar anchors where comparison is more useful than novelty.
map_note: Four loaded landing events; most rapid force comes from planted/supporting tasks.
next_job: Consolidate repeatability with low-amplitude/contact-controlled force tasks and a small strength dose.
handoff: Review actual handling, selected substitutions and recovery if reported, then finalize Class 10 and save its audit/state before continuing.

final_review: Checked that each nonflight row contains a real rapid lower-limb force task rather than conditioning or upper-body filler. Loaded flight is limited to four events; secure-handling and lighter/no-load routes are explicit. Thirty nonflight force efforts remain distinct from jump contacts and from primary strength repetitions. Guided/loaded variants are labeled honestly, with no automatic load progression.
